column3: The Hebrew reads “Saul was a son of a year when he became king, and two years he reigned over Israel”; NKJV renders “Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years,” joining the verse to verse 2.
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV follows the shorter Hebrew text, without the longer Septuagint wording.
NKJV has “Gibeah of Benjamin,” where the Hebrew has “Geba of Benjamin.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV renders the second מַחֲרֵשָׁתוֹ (“plowshare”) as “sickle.”
NKJV gives the charge as “a pim” (the Hebrew weight word), and renders “three-pronged fork” as “forks.”
